concepts.name: Polynomials and their values
concepts.description: A polynomial is a sum of terms cxⁿ with whole-number powers; its degree is the highest power. p(a) means put a for every x. Multiplying adds degrees.

concepts.name: The remainder theorem
concepts.description: p(x) divided by x − a leaves p(a); divided by ax − b it leaves p(b/a). One substitution replaces a long division.

concepts.name: The factor theorem
concepts.description: x − a is a factor of p(x) exactly when p(a) = 0. A missing coefficient comes from setting the value (or the given remainder) equal; two factors give two equations.

concepts.name: Dividing polynomials
concepts.description: Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder, with the remainder of lower degree than the divisor. Synthetic division divides by x − a in one row.

concepts.name: Roots and coefficients
concepts.description: For ax² + bx + c: α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a. For ax³ + bx² + cx + d: Σα = −b/a, Σαβ = c/a, αβγ = −d/a. Symmetric expressions follow from these.

concepts.name: Real roots from a graph
concepts.description: Real roots are where the graph meets the x-axis. A degree-n polynomial has at most n real roots and at most n − 1 turning points; an odd degree always has at least one. A sign change between two values traps a root.

concepts.name: Remainder on a quadratic divisor
concepts.description: Dividing by (x − a)(x − b) leaves a remainder rx + s of degree at most 1, found from p(a) = ra + s and p(b) = rb + s.

concepts.name: New equations from old roots
concepts.description: Equations whose roots are kα, α + h or 1/α come from substituting x/k, x − h, or reversing the coefficients. Expressions such as 1/α + 1/β are written in the sum and product.

formulas.title: Value and degree of a polynomial
formulas.prompt: What does p(a) mean, and what is the degree of a polynomial?
formulas.formula:
p(a) = the value of p(x) with x = a
Degree = highest power of x with a non-zero coefficient
formulas.explanation: Substitute the number for every x and keep the signs. When two polynomials are multiplied, their degrees add.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading 2x³ at x = 2 as (2 × 2)³ = 64 instead of 2 × 8 = 16.

formulas.title: Remainder theorem
formulas.prompt: What remainder does p(x) leave when divided by x − a, or by ax − b?
formulas.formula:
p(x) ÷ (x − a) leaves p(a)
p(x) ÷ (ax − b) leaves p(b/a)

variables.meaning: the number that makes the divisor zero

formulas.explanation: Write p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + r and put x = a: the first part becomes 0, leaving r = p(a).
formulas.commonMistake: Putting x = 3 for the divisor x + 3; the divisor is zero at x = −3.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the remainder when x³ + 5 is divided by x + 2.

formulas.title: Factor theorem
formulas.prompt: How do you test whether x − a is a factor of p(x)?
formulas.formula: (x − a) is a factor of p(x)  ⇔  p(a) = 0
formulas.explanation: A factor divides exactly, so the remainder p(a) must be zero. Setting p(a) = 0 also finds a missing coefficient.
formulas.example: x³ + 3x² − 4 at x = −2: −8 + 12 − 4 = 0, so (x + 2) is a factor
formulas.commonMistake: Testing p(2) for the factor x + 2.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Is x − 1 a factor of x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6?

formulas.title: Division of polynomials
formulas.prompt: How are the dividend, divisor, quotient and remainder related?
formulas.formula: p(x) = d(x) × q(x) + r(x),  degree of r < degree of d
formulas.explanation: Dividing by a linear divisor leaves a constant; dividing by a quadratic leaves at most a linear remainder.
formulas.commonMistake: Leaving a remainder whose degree is not less than the divisor’s.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A polynomial divided by x − 1 gives quotient x² + 2 and remainder 5. What is it?

formulas.title: Roots of a quadratic
formulas.prompt: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α and β, what are α + β and αβ?
formulas.explanation: ax² + bx + c = a(x − α)(x − β); comparing coefficients gives both at once.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the sum and product of the roots of 3x² + 6x − 9 = 0.

formulas.title: Roots of a cubic
formulas.prompt: For ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0 with roots α, β, γ, what are Σα, Σαβ and αβγ?
formulas.formula:
α + β + γ = −b/a
αβ + βγ + γα = c/a
αβγ = −d/a
formulas.explanation: The signs alternate: minus, plus, minus. The relations hold for all three roots, real or not.
formulas.commonMistake: Giving the product as d/a; for a cubic it is −d/a.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the product of the roots of 2x³ + x² − 5x + 4 = 0.

formulas.title: Roots and turning points
formulas.prompt: How many real roots and turning points can a polynomial of degree n have?
formulas.formula:
At most n real roots and at most n − 1 turning points
Odd degree ⇒ at least one real root
p(a) and p(b) of opposite signs ⇒ a root between a and b
formulas.explanation: Each real root is a point where the graph meets the x-axis. An odd-degree graph runs from −∞ to +∞, so it must cross.
formulas.example: x³ − 3x + 1: p(0) = 1, p(1) = −1, so a root lies between 0 and 1
formulas.commonMistake: Thinking a cubic always has three real roots; x³ + x has only one.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Can a polynomial of degree 4 have 5 real roots?

formulas.title: Remainder on (x − a)(x − b)
formulas.prompt: How do you find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − a)(x − b)?
formulas.formula:
Remainder = rx + s, where
ra + s = p(a),  rb + s = p(b)
formulas.explanation: The remainder has degree below 2. Both a and b make the divisor zero, giving two equations for r and s.
formulas.commonMistake: Expecting a constant remainder from a quadratic divisor.
formulas.applicationPrompt: p(2) = 7 and p(−1) = 1. Find the remainder on division by (x − 2)(x + 1).

formulas.title: Equation with changed roots
formulas.prompt: From p(x) = 0 with roots α, β, how do you get the equation whose roots are kα, α + h or 1/α?
formulas.formula:
Roots kα: p(x/k) = 0
Roots α + h: p(x − h) = 0
Roots 1/α: reverse the coefficients
formulas.explanation: If x = kα then x/k = α is a root of p, so p(x/k) = 0. The same idea gives the other two.
formulas.commonMistake: Doubling only the sum and forgetting that the product is multiplied by 4.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Form the equation whose roots are the reciprocals of the roots of 2x² − 6x + 1 = 0.

formulas.title: Remainder on x − 1 and x + 1
formulas.prompt: What is the quickest way to the remainder on division by x − 1 or by x + 1?
formulas.formula:
p(1) = sum of the coefficients
p(−1) = (even-power coefficients) − (odd-power coefficients)
formulas.explanation: At x = 1 every power is 1; at x = −1 odd powers become −1.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the remainder when x²⁰ + 3x¹⁵ − 2 is divided by x + 1.

formulas.title: Synthetic division
formulas.prompt: How do you divide by x − a without long division?
formulas.formula:
Write the coefficients (0 for a missing power).
Bring the first down; multiply by a, add to the next; repeat.
Last number = remainder; the rest = quotient
formulas.explanation: Each step is one multiplication and one addition, so a cubic takes three steps.
formulas.commonMistake: Skipping the 0 for a missing power, which shifts every later number.

formulas.title: Sum of squares of the roots
formulas.prompt: How do you find α² + β² without finding the roots?
formulas.formula:
α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ
α² + β² + γ² = (Σα)² − 2Σαβ
formulas.explanation: Squaring the sum adds twice every product, so subtract it back.

formulas.title: Where to look for integer roots
formulas.prompt: Which numbers can be integer roots of x³ + bx² + cx + d with whole-number coefficients?
formulas.formula: An integer root must divide the constant term d
formulas.explanation: If r is a root then r(r² + br + c) = −d, so r divides d. Test only those divisors.
formulas.commonMistake: Testing numbers that do not divide the constant term.
formulas.applicationPrompt: List the candidates for an integer root of x³ + 2x² − x − 2.

levels.title: Remainders Without Long Division
levels.description: Values of a polynomial, the remainder and factor theorems, and what the coefficients say about the roots.

blocks.title: A polynomial and its value
blocks.body: p(x) = 2x³ − 5x² + 3x − 7 is a polynomial of degree 3, the highest power of x. Its value at x = 2 comes from putting 2 for every x: p(2) = 16 − 20 + 6 − 7 = −5. Work each term on its own: 2x³ at x = 2 is 2 × 8, not (2 × 2)³.

blocks.title: The remainder is a value
blocks.body:
Divide p(x) by x − a and write p(x) = (x − a) × q(x) + r. Now put x = a: the first part becomes 0, so r = p(a).

So the remainder when x³ − 4x² + 2x + 9 is divided by x − 3 is just p(3) = 27 − 36 + 6 + 9 = 6. No long division is needed.

blocks.title: Remainder and factor theorems
blocks.body:
p(x) ÷ (x − a) leaves p(a)
(x − a) is a factor ⇔ p(a) = 0
blocks.caption: For a divisor ax − b, use x = b/a: the remainder is p(b/a). On the graph, the remainder is the height of the curve at x = a; a factor is a point where the curve meets the x-axis.

blocks.title: The coefficients know the roots
blocks.body: If α and β are the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0, then α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a. A cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0 has α + β + γ = −b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a and αβγ = −d/a. The signs alternate: minus, plus, minus.
Watch the sign of the divisor: x + 2 is x − (−2), so put x = −2, not 2.

levels.title: Polynomial Formulas
levels.description: Values, the remainder and factor theorems, division, and the relations between roots and coefficients.

levels.title: Direct Substitution
levels.description: Values, remainders, a factor test and the sum of roots, one step each.

levels.title: Missing Coefficients and Division
levels.description: Find a coefficient from a factor or a remainder, divide synthetically, and use the roots of a cubic.

levels.title: Two Conditions and Graphs
levels.description: Two factors at once, fractional divisors, rebuilding a dividend, and counting where a graph meets the axis.

levels.title: Advanced: Quadratic Divisors and New Roots
levels.description: The linear remainder left by a quadratic divisor, and equations whose roots are changed versions of the old ones.

blocks.title: A quadratic divisor leaves a linear remainder
blocks.body: When the divisor has degree 2, the remainder has degree at most 1: p(x) = (x − a)(x − b)q(x) + rx + s. Putting x = a and x = b gives ra + s = p(a) and rb + s = p(b): two equations for r and s.

blocks.title: Remainder on (x − a)(x − b)
blocks.body: r = (p(a) − p(b)) ÷ (a − b),  s = p(a) − ra
blocks.caption: Example: p(1) = 5 and p(3) = 11 give r = 3 and s = 2, so the remainder is 3x + 2.

blocks.title: New equations from old roots
blocks.body:
For roots 2α and 2β, put x/2 for x. For roots α + 1 and β + 1, put x − 1 for x. For roots 1/α and 1/β, write the coefficients in reverse: 2x² − 6x + 1 = 0 becomes x² − 6x + 2 = 0.

Often you only need the new sum and product: for 2α and 2β they are 2(α + β) and 4αβ.
Symmetric expressions such as α² + β², 1/α + 1/β or α³ + β³ can always be written using α + β and αβ, so you never need the roots themselves.

levels.title: Challenge: Remainders and Roots
levels.description: Quadratic divisors, changed roots, products of roots and roots read from a table.

questions.question: If p(x) = 2x³ − 5x² + 3x − 7, what is p(2)?
questions.method: Substitute, then work each term separately.

hints.text: Work out 2³ first, then multiply by 2.

questions.question: Find the remainder when x³ − 4x² + 2x + 9 is divided by x − 3.
questions.explanation: By the remainder theorem the remainder is p(3) = 27 − 36 + 6 + 9 = 6. No long division is needed.
solutionSteps: The divisor x − 3 is zero at x = 3.
questions.method: Remainder = p(a) for the divisor x − a.

hints.text: Which value of x makes x − 3 zero?
Work out p(3).

questions.question: (x + 2) is a factor of x³ + 3x² − 4.
questions.explanation: x + 2 is zero at x = −2, and p(−2) = −8 + 12 − 4 = 0. A zero remainder means x + 2 is a factor (x³ + 3x² − 4 = (x + 2)²(x − 1)).
solutionSteps: Remainder 0, so it is a factor: true.
questions.method: Test p at the value that makes the divisor zero.

hints.text: For the divisor x + 2, put x = −2.

questions.question: When a polynomial p(x) is divided by 2x − 3, the remainder is:
questions.explanation: The divisor 2x − 3 is zero at x = 3/2. Writing p(x) = (2x − 3)q(x) + r and putting x = 3/2 leaves r = p(3/2).
questions.method: Find the zero of the divisor.

hints.text: Which x makes 2x − 3 equal to 0?
Solve 2x = 3.

commonMistakes: Using only the constant 3 and ignoring the 2 in front of x.

questions.question: What is the sum of the roots of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0?
questions.explanation: Sum of roots = −b/a = −(−7)/2 = 7/2. Check: the roots are 3 and 1/2, and 3 + 1/2 = 7/2.
questions.method: Sum of roots = −b/a.

hints.text: Use −b/a; here b = −7.
Do not forget to divide by a = 2.

commonMistakes: Giving the product c/a = 3/2; forgetting to divide by a.

questions.question: If x − 2 is a factor of x³ + kx² − 5x + 6, find k.
questions.explanation: x − 2 is a factor, so p(2) = 0: 8 + 4k − 10 + 6 = 0, so 4k + 4 = 0 and k = −1. Check: x³ − x² − 5x + 6 at x = 2 is 8 − 4 − 10 + 6 = 0.
questions.method: Factor theorem: set p(a) = 0 and solve for the unknown.

hints.text: A factor leaves remainder 0, so p(2) = 0.

questions.question: When 3x³ + ax² − 4x + 1 is divided by x + 1, the remainder is 7. Find a.
questions.explanation: The remainder is p(−1) = −3 + a + 4 + 1 = a + 2. Setting a + 2 = 7 gives a = 5.
questions.method: Remainder theorem, then solve for the coefficient.

hints.text: Put x = −1, the zero of x + 1.
−4x at x = −1 is +4.

commonMistakes: Taking −4x as −4 at x = −1, which gives a = 13; dropping the constant 1, which gives a = 6.

questions.question: Divide x³ + 2x² − 5x + 7 by x − 2. What is the constant term of the quotient?
questions.explanation: Synthetic division with 2: bring down 1; 1 × 2 + 2 = 4; 4 × 2 − 5 = 3; 3 × 2 + 7 = 13. The quotient is x² + 4x + 3 and the remainder 13, so the constant term is 3.
questions.method: Synthetic division: multiply by 2, add, repeat.

hints.text: Write 1, 2, −5, 7 and bring the 1 down.
The last number of the row is the remainder, not part of the quotient.

commonMistakes: Giving the remainder 13 as the constant term.

questions.question: Put the steps in order to divide 2x³ − 3x² + 5 by x − 2 by synthetic division.

steps.text: Write the coefficients 2, −3, 0, 5 (0 for the missing x term) and the number 2
Multiply 2 × 2 = 4 and add to −3 to get 1
Multiply 1 × 2 = 2 and add to 0 to get 2
Multiply 2 × 2 = 4 and add to 5 to get 9, the remainder

questions.explanation: Synthetic division works on the coefficients alone. Each step multiplies the last number by 2 and adds it to the next coefficient. The final number, 9, is the remainder: check p(2) = 16 − 12 + 5 = 9.
questions.method: Bring down, multiply, add, repeat.

hints.text: The missing x term still needs a place.
Every step after the first is "multiply by 2, then add".

commonMistakes: Leaving out the 0 for the missing x term.

questions.question: If α, β and γ are the roots of x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 = 0, what is α² + β² + γ²?
questions.explanation: Σα = 6 and Σαβ = 11, so α² + β² + γ² = 6² − 2 × 11 = 36 − 22 = 14. Check: the roots are 1, 2, 3 and 1 + 4 + 9 = 14.
questions.method: Square the sum and subtract twice the pair sum.

hints.text: (α + β + γ)² = α² + β² + γ² + 2(αβ + βγ + γα).
Σα = 6 and Σαβ = 11.

questions.question: p(x) is a cubic polynomial with real coefficients. Select ALL the statements that must be true.

options.text: Its graph meets the x-axis at least once
It has exactly three real roots
Its graph has at most two turning points
Its graph meets the x-axis at most three times
If p(1) and p(2) are both positive, no root lies between 1 and 2

questions.explanation: A cubic runs from −∞ to +∞ (or the reverse), so it crosses the axis at least once, and degree 3 allows at most 3 roots and at most 2 turning points. It need not have three real roots: x³ + x has one. Two positive values do not rule out a root between them: the curve can dip below the axis and come back, crossing twice.
solutionSteps: (b) x³ + x has one real root: false.
(c) at most n − 1 = 2 turning points: true.
(e) the curve may cross twice between 1 and 2: false.
questions.method: Degree n: at most n roots and n − 1 turns; odd degree: at least one root.

hints.text: Think of x³ + x and of x³ − x.
A sign change proves a root, but no sign change proves nothing.

commonMistakes: Assuming every cubic has three real roots.

questions.question: What is the coefficient of x² in (x² − 3x + 2)(2x + 5)?
questions.explanation: x² arises in two ways: x² × 5 = 5x² and (−3x) × 2x = −6x². Together 5 − 6 = −1. The full product is 2x³ − x² − 11x + 10.
questions.method: Pick out only the pairs of terms whose powers add to 2.

hints.text: Which pairs of terms multiply to give x²?
There are two: x² × 5 and (−3x) × 2x.

questions.question: Both x − 2 and x + 3 are factors of x³ + ax² + bx − 12. Find a − b.
questions.method: One equation from each factor, then solve the pair.

hints.text: Each factor gives one equation: p(2) = 0 and p(−3) = 0.
Add 2a + b = 2 and 3a − b = 13.

commonMistakes: Using p(3) for the factor x + 3.

questions.question: Find the remainder when 4x³ − 2x² + x − 5 is divided by 2x − 1.
questions.method: Remainder = p(b/a) for the divisor ax − b.

hints.text: Solve 2x − 1 = 0.

questions.question: A polynomial divided by x² + 1 gives quotient 2x − 3 and remainder x + 4. What is the coefficient of x in the polynomial?
questions.explanation: Dividend = (x² + 1)(2x − 3) + (x + 4) = 2x³ − 3x² + 2x − 3 + x + 4 = 2x³ − 3x² + 3x + 1. The coefficient of x is 3.
questions.method: Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder.

hints.text: Rebuild the dividend: divisor × quotient + remainder.
The x terms are 2x (from 1 × 2x) and x (from the remainder).

commonMistakes: Forgetting to add the remainder and answering 2.

questions.question: The length and breadth, in metres, of a rectangular plot in Pune are the roots of x² − 17x + 60 = 0. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Length + breadth = sum of roots = 17, so the perimeter is 2 × 17 = 34 m. (The roots are 12 and 5, and the area is the product, 60 m².)
questions.method: Use the sum of roots directly; no need to solve.

hints.text: Perimeter needs l + b.
l + b is the sum of the roots, −b/a.

commonMistakes: Giving l + b = 17 m without doubling.

questions.question: Match each polynomial with the number of points where its graph meets the x-axis.
questions.explanation: x² + 4 is always at least 4, so it never meets the axis. x² − 6x + 9 = (x − 3)² touches at x = 3. x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) crosses at 2 and 3. x³ − 4x = x(x − 2)(x + 2) crosses at −2, 0 and 2.
questions.method: Factorise and count the distinct real roots.

hints.text: Factorise each one where you can.
A squared factor touches the axis once.

questions.question: A polynomial p(x) leaves remainder 5 when divided by x − 1 and remainder 11 when divided by x − 3. What remainder does it leave when divided by (x − 1)(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: The remainder is rx + s with r + s = p(1) = 5 and 3r + s = p(3) = 11. Subtracting, 2r = 6, so r = 3 and s = 2: the remainder is 3x + 2.
questions.method: Write the remainder as rx + s and use both zeros of the divisor.

hints.text: A quadratic divisor leaves a remainder of the form rx + s.
Put x = 1 and x = 3.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to divide 6 by 2: 6x − 1; adding the two remainders: 16.

questions.question: α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0. Which equation has roots 2α and 2β?
questions.explanation: New sum = 2(α + β) = 10; new product = 4αβ = 12. So the equation is x² − 10x + 12 = 0. (Equivalently, put x/2 for x: x²/4 − 5x/2 + 3 = 0, times 4.)
questions.method: New equation: x² − (new sum)x + (new product) = 0.

hints.text: Find α + β and αβ first.
The product of 2α and 2β is 4αβ, not 2αβ.

commonMistakes: Doubling the product instead of multiplying by 4: x² − 10x + 6 = 0.

questions.question: α and β are the roots of 2x² − 6x + 1 = 0. Find 1/α + 1/β.
questions.explanation: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ). Here α + β = 6/2 = 3 and αβ = 1/2, so the value is 3 ÷ 1/2 = 6.
questions.method: Combine over a common denominator, then use sum and product.

hints.text: Add the fractions: (β + α)/(αβ).

questions.question: When x¹⁰¹ + 2 is divided by x² − 1, the remainder is rx + s. Find s.
questions.explanation: x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1). p(1) = 1 + 2 = 3 gives r + s = 3; p(−1) = −1 + 2 = 1 gives −r + s = 1. Adding, 2s = 4, so s = 2 (and r = 1): the remainder is x + 2.
questions.method: Use the zeros 1 and −1 of the divisor.

hints.text: Factorise x² − 1.
(−1)¹⁰¹ = −1 because 101 is odd.

questions.question: The product of the three roots (real or not) of 2x³ − 4x² + 6x − 8 = 0 is 4.
questions.explanation: For ax³ + bx² + cx + d, αβγ = −d/a = −(−8)/2 = 4. The relation holds whether or not the roots are real.
questions.method: Product of roots of a cubic = −d/a.

hints.text: For a cubic the product is −d/a, not d/a.

questions.question: α, β and γ are the roots of x³ − 3x² + 2x − 1 = 0. Find 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ.
questions.explanation: 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ = (βγ + γα + αβ)/(αβγ). Σαβ = c/a = 2 and αβγ = −d/a = 1, so the value is 2/1 = 2.
questions.method: Common denominator αβγ, numerator Σαβ.

hints.text: Write the three fractions over αβγ.
The numerator becomes αβ + βγ + γα.

commonMistakes: Using the sum of roots, 3, as the numerator.
Taking αβγ = d/a = −1, which gives −2; turning the fraction upside down: 1/2.

questions.question: p(x) is a cubic polynomial with the values in the table. How many real roots does p(x) have?
questions.explanation: The sign changes from −2 to −1 (− to +), from 0 to 1 (+ to −) and from 1 to 2 (− to +), so a root lies in each of these three gaps. A cubic has at most three real roots, so it has exactly 3. (This is p(x) = x³ − 3x + 1.)
solutionSteps: Three sign changes → at least three roots.
A cubic has at most three → exactly 3.
questions.method: Count sign changes, then cap by the degree.

hints.text: Look for neighbouring values of opposite sign.
A cubic cannot have more than three real roots.

commonMistakes: Counting only the gap from 0 to 1.
Saying it cannot be determined, forgetting the cap of three.
